privacy.title: Privacy & Data Access
privacy.descSimple: We physically cannot read your chats or share metadata with third parties. Gossip incorporates post-quantum security: every message is sealed with hybrid keys (ML-KEM Kyber + X25519) on your device. Even future quantum supercomputers won't decrypt traffic captured today.
privacy.descGeek: Full post-quantum end-to-end encryption with PQ-MLS & PQXDH (NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768 lattice Z_q[X]/(X^256+1) + Curve25519). Resilient against Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later attacks. Key derivation via HKDF-SHA256 Combiner. Keys never leave the device.
privacy.footer: Where keys are stored: Exclusively on your device (Zero-Knowledge)

openness.title: Openness & Sovereignty
openness.descSimple: Gossip client source code is 100% open and auditable — anyone can inspect our algorithms. The project is shielded by an author license to prevent Big Tech monopolies from stealing and monetizing our tech in proprietary black boxes.
openness.descGeek: Two-tier BSL 1.1 / Open-Core architecture: 100% open client codebase for verifiable cryptographic audits and Reproducible Builds. Server is protected by Air-Gapped Ed25519 licensing and Attestation Guard.
openness.footerPublic: Public client repository open for independent security audit

monetization.title: How We Make Money
monetization.descSimple: We have no oligarch sponsors or ad brokers requiring your data. Core messaging is free forever. We sustain development through voluntary Premium patron subscriptions with custom themes, shaders, and animated backgrounds.
monetization.descGeek: Infrastructure is funded through premium digital asset sales and patron tiers. Integrated anonymous crypto checkout (zero KYC for micro-tiers) alongside standard fiat channels for P2P contributions.

recovery.title: Forgot password? Protection against SIM-Swap attacks
recovery.subtitle: In standard messengers, SMS resets let attackers or carriers read your entire history. In Gossip, servers never have your keys, so recovery is guaranteed mathematically.
recovery.seedDesc: Generated hardware-side on your device during profile creation. The server never sees these words.
recovery.seedProcessDesc: If you forget your password or lose your phone: enter these 12 words on your new device. Private ML-KEM-768 and Curve25519 keys are recalculated locally, your local message database is decrypted, and a new SRP verifier is generated for the server.
recovery.devicesDesc: If you have an active session on your laptop or tablet, your phone password can be updated instantly with zero server involvement.
recovery.deviceStep1Desc: Desktop client renders a dynamic QR code containing a single-use X25519 public key. Phone scans the code and establishes an encrypted P2P tunnel.
recovery.deviceStep2Desc: Chat encryption keys are transferred directly between your devices in encrypted form. Server acts only as a blind relay.

recovery.simDesc: What happens if an attacker clones your SIM card or compromises your carrier account?

recovery.simGossip1: Attacker intercepts SMS or tries to reset account.

faq.title: Honest Answers to Tough Questions
faq.subtitle: We communicate openly with our community without corporate jargon or evasiveness
faq.q1: Is it legal to communicate privately and use end-to-end encryption?
faq.a1Simple: Absolutely legal. Article 12 of the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights guarantees everyone the right to privacy and correspondence secrecy. Privacy is a fundamental human right. Gossip mathematically protects your sovereign personal space.
faq.a1Geek: Legal basis: Art. 12 UDHR (UN), GDPR, and Privacy by Design standards. End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) is the recognized global standard for information security. Zero-Knowledge architecture guarantees encryption keys never leave the owner's hardware.
faq.q2: Can government agencies or administrators read my conversations?
faq.a2Simple: Physically and mathematically impossible. Private chats are E2EE protected. Decryption keys are generated strictly on your device and are never sent to our servers. We have zero backdoors and zero technical capability to read your data.
faq.a2Geek: We utilize X3DH / Double Ratchet and MLS (Message Layer Security) key exchange on X25519 (ECDH) with HKDF-SHA256 derivation. A hybrid post-quantum ML-KEM-768 (Kyber) layer is actively being phased in. On-disk databases are encrypted via SQLCipher (AES-256-GCM). Cloud storage (ScyllaDB) holds only opaque cryptographic ciphertext.
faq.q3: What happens if Gossip servers are blocked or the internet goes down?
faq.a3Simple: You will keep communicating. Gossip has built-in DPI censorship circumvention, and if the internet shuts down entirely, the app automatically switches to off-grid BLE Mesh radio mode between nearby smartphones.
faq.a3Geek: For DPI circumvention, we use a custom Fake TLS Proxy wrapping WebSocket traffic as standard HTTPS on port 443. In total network blackouts, an autonomous Bluetooth Low Energy Mesh protocol engages (GATT UUID 0xFA21, Store & Forward with TTL and deduplication).
faq.q4: How does Gossip monetize? Will my data ever be sold?
faq.a4Simple: We never sell your data, contacts, or chat history to advertisers — we simply do not have that data. Gossip is sustained through transparent Premium subscriptions (custom themes, animated backgrounds, audio transcription) and Enterprise solutions.
faq.a4Geek: Zero telemetry: no Google Analytics, Firebase Analytics, or Facebook SDKs in client apps. Gossip Premium is activated via Chaumian Blind Signatures, completely unlinking payments from user identities.
faq.q5: Why is there a Proof-of-Work requirement before authorization?
faq.a5Simple: It is an invisible mathematical captcha protecting the network from botnets and spammers trying to flood the servers with millions of fake requests.
faq.a5Geek: Proof-of-Work requires clients to find a SHA-256 nonce with target leading zeros before dispatching requests. The server validates in O(1) time, while spammers face prohibitive computational and energy costs, rendering DDoS attacks economically unviable.
faq.q6: How does the Offline Radar and Mesh Radio work with no cellular or internet?
faq.a6Simple: If you are in deep wilderness, mountains, or during a grid outage — smartphones discover each other over Bluetooth, display distance on an interactive radar, and relay encrypted packets hop-by-hop across neighbors until reaching the recipient.
faq.a6Geek: Operates a native 2.4 GHz BLE Mesh protocol (GATT 0xFA21, characteristics 0xFA22/0xFA23/0xFA24) combining Advertising and Scanning roles. Distance is estimated via RSSI Path Loss. Packets are E2EE encrypted and forwarded hop-by-hop (Hop Count <= 7), preventing intermediate relays from inspecting payloads.
faq.q7: What is the Sovereign Economic Layer (SEL) and ZK-Trust ('Digital Lawyer')?
faq.a7Simple: It is a built-in platform for secure transactions without banks, middlemen, or fraud risk. You can prove your solvency without revealing your balance or wallet address (ZKP), while smart escrow releases funds only when independent oracles verify physical delivery.
faq.a7Geek: ZK-Trust Protocol (ZKTP) and Delivery-versus-Payment (DvP) smart contracts on TON using Halo2 ZK-SNARKs. Provides Proof of Solvency and Proof of Deposit Age against flash loans, integrating 3-tier oracle verification (AIS maritime satellites, SGS inspection, TLSNotary 2PC-TLS).
faq.q8: Is the project open source and where can I inspect the code?
faq.a8Simple: Yes, Gossip source code is completely open on GitHub. Anyone or any cybersecurity researcher can inspect every line of code, build the app independently, and verify there are zero backdoors or hidden tracking.
faq.a8Geek: The repository at github.com/up1t3/gossip-public contains complete source code for web, mobile (Capacitor Android), and desktop (Electron) clients, the cryptographic core (X3DH, Double Ratchet, AES-256-GCM, MLS), the native BLE Mesh plugin, and smart contracts. Official APK builds are verifiable via public SHA-256 certificate fingerprints.
faq.q9: How do I recover access if I lose my phone or suffer a SIM-Swap attack?
faq.a9Simple: In traditional messengers, an SMS intercept grants the hacker full access to your chats. In Gossip, SIM-swapping yields a blank profile: without your password or 12-word seed phrase, past messages are mathematically impossible to decrypt.
faq.a9Geek: Zero-Knowledge recovery powered by BIP-39 12-word mnemonics with local PBKDF2/Argon2 key derivation. Server authentication utilizes SRP-6a (Secure Remote Password): passwords and master seeds are never transmitted over the network.
